finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id ignores the return value of authorized(), which returns a boolean and does not throw. Any authenticated user can delete any project they don't own. Separately, a nonexistent id gives project undefined, so the call throws a TypeError and returns a 500, which is a minor issue.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (req.user) sending DELETE /projects/<victim project id>

trace.note: Route handler for DELETE /projects/:id; the id comes from the URL and is attacker-controlled
Project is fetched by id with no ownership scoping
authorized(req.user, project) is called as a bare statement, so its boolean result is discarded
authorized() only returns true or false and never throws, so the check has no effect
By contrast, PUT /projects/:id/name uses authorize(), which throws a 403, so that route is protected

finding.guards_checked: Searched the file for middleware or router-level authorization. There is none in api.js. Authentication of req.user is assumed to happen upstream, and it does not enforce ownership. The return value of authorized() is not used. The fix is to use authorize() or to check `if (!authorized(...))`.
